questions.label: Workspace
questions.prompt: You get to design your workspace. Pick the closest fit.

options.label: A studio with one long table and your tools laid out
A quiet office with a door that closes
No desk at all — you're rarely in the same place twice
A shared kitchen, with a corkboard for half-finished ideas

questions.label: Meeting
questions.prompt: How do you most hate to meet?

options.label: The standing weekly that could be an email
The pitch meeting where the room has already decided
The 1:1 that turns into a confession booth
The town hall where your work is mentioned in passing

questions.label: Deadline
questions.prompt: What's the best kind of deadline?

options.label: The one that was yesterday — you finish under pressure
The one that's three months out, for the slow craft
None — you set your own and quietly keep them
The one a stakeholder will notice if you miss

questions.label: The trade-off
questions.prompt: Pay doubles, but the work is less yours. You...

options.label: Take it for a season, keep the craft private
Decline — the work is the point
Negotiate so the work stays half yours
Take it, and start the real thing on the side

questions.label: Praise
questions.prompt: The praise that lands best is...

options.label: A public thank-you, in front of people who matter
A private note, years later, from someone you helped
A repeat customer who comes back without a coupon
The kind no one writes down, but everyone uses
Mostly you, with one sharp collaborator
Two of you, doing everything
A small pod of four to seven, with shared rituals
A loose guild that comes together for projects

questions.label: Hard part
questions.prompt: The hardest part of a job is...

options.label: Politics — who's upstream of whom
Precision — the part that has to be right by Tuesday
Ambiguity — five equally good ways, no map
Loneliness — being the only one who cares about the small thing

questions.label: After hours
questions.prompt: After a good day at work, you...

options.label: Tinker on a side project until it gets good
Read something that has nothing to do with the work
Talk to people who don't know what your job is
Walk until the day's shape is gone

questions.label: Monday morning
questions.prompt: Monday morning. What's the most you hope for?

options.label: Predictable, with one small surprise
A new project you'd choose again
A chance to be useful in a way only you would notice
Wide-open time, and the discipline to use it

archetypes.label: Artisan
archetypes.tagline: The work has to be right, and you'd rather do it slowly than badly.
archetypes.blindSpot: Craft can become a private religion when the room needs a finished thing.

archetypes.label: Pioneer
archetypes.tagline: Builds the road by walking it, and prefers the path that hasn't been drawn yet.
archetypes.blindSpot: Pioneering can mistake novelty for value when a tired road was fine.

archetypes.label: Steward
archetypes.tagline: Keeps the institution honest — the kind that notices what's quietly drifting.
archetypes.blindSpot: Stewardship can become the thing no one thanks you for, until it breaks.

archetypes.label: Scholar
archetypes.tagline: Measures twice, returns to the source, and treats the work as a long argument.
archetypes.blindSpot: Scholarly patience can read as hesitation when the room needs a verdict.

archetypes.label: Diplomat
archetypes.tagline: Holds the room together, translates between floors, and remembers who said what.
archetypes.blindSpot: Diplomacy can keep the peace past the point where a clean break would help.

archetypes.label: Maverick
archetypes.tagline: Wants the wide-open room, the stubborn brief, and the permission to break the format.
archetypes.blindSpot: Independence can leave a small mess for someone else to clean up on Monday.
